pyodbc running under Python_3 doesn't accept those.

I get the impression that the mysql+pyodbc dialect tried valiantly to work around the (admitted) deficiencies in pyodbc's Unicode handling prior to version 4. Now, if the dialect could simply do the equivalent of

```python
cnxn = pyodbc.connect(connection_string)
cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_CHAR, encoding='utf-8')
cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_WCHAR, encoding='utf-8')
cnxn.setencoding(encoding='utf-8')
```

(as documented [here](https://github.com/mkleehammer/pyodbc/wiki/Unicode#mysql-and-postgresql)) then that might simplify things considerably, at least for Python_3.

OK if it's getting bytes in py3k there's a flag to set:

supports_unicode_statements = True

looks like the mysql driver is hardcoding to false. likely can just set it to true as it is hardcoded to true in the base, meaning that works on py2k also.

is there any modern use case for mysql + pyodbc ?

> looks like the mysql driver is hardcoding to false

Yes, indeed. After I changed

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/2c34d2503a17316cae3282192405b9b9d60df6fe/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/pyodbc.py#L43

```python
    supports_unicode_statements = True
```

> is there any modern use case for mysql + pyodbc ?

Clearly there is not an overwhelming demand for it. I was just curious to see if it could be a viable alternative given that comments in the SQLAlchemy user documentation and code refer to

http://code.google.com/p/pyodbc/issues/detail?id=25

which is an issue from over ten years ago.

The other potential source of interest is from people who already work with MySQL via ODBC and would prefer to use pyodbc instead of installing a "whole other thing" (for DB-API) when they already have pyodbc and MySQL Connector/ODBC installed.

issue.title: set up utf-8 directives for mysql-pyodbc
issue.body:
(Further to #4869, specifically [this comment](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4869#issuecomment-536322193).) 

I have been able to tweak the mysql+pyodbc dialect and requirements to eliminate most of the failures in the test suite (currently "Tests failed: 11, passed: 126, ignored: 133") but I have one more hurdle. It involves the Unicode encoding used by MySQL Connector/ODBC.

As explained in the pyodbc wiki [Unicode article](https://github.com/mkleehammer/pyodbc/wiki/Unicode#mysql-and-postgresql), MySQL ODBC tends to use UTF-8 exclusively while the default for pyodbc is UTF-16. The fix is to explicitly set the encoding after the Connection object is created, e.g.,

```python
# Python 3.x
cnxn = pyodbc.connect(connection_string)
cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_CHAR, encoding='utf-8')
cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_WCHAR, encoding='utf-8')
cnxn.setencoding(encoding='utf-8')
```

I have verified that with my current test setup the code ...

```python
import pyodbc

cnxn = pyodbc.connect("DSN=mysql_sqla")

# cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_CHAR, encoding='utf-8')
# cnxn.setdecoding(pyodbc.SQL_WCHAR, encoding='utf-8')
# cnxn.setencoding(encoding='utf-8')

crsr = cnxn.cursor()

crsr.execute("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE foo (txt varchar(255))")

txt = "Alors vous imaginez ma 🐍 surprise, au lever du jour, quand une drôle de petite 🐍 voix m’a réveillé."
crsr.execute("INSERT INTO foo (txt) VALUES (?)", txt)

result = crsr.execute("SELECT txt FROM foo").fetchval()
print(result)
```

... fails with ...

```
pyodbc.Error: ('HY000', "[HY000] [MySQL][ODBC 8.0(w) Driver][mysqld-5.7.27-0ubuntu0.18.04.1]Incorrect string value: '\\xF0\\x9F\\x90\\x8D s...' for column 'txt' at row 1 (1366) (SQLExecDirectW)")
```

... but if I uncomment the setdecoding/setencoding lines then the code works fine.

So, I'm looking for the hook in the mysql+pyodbc dialect where I can specify those additional post-connect directives.

Any pointers greatly appreciated.
